newsitem.title: CANADA: Final Senate votes set on Canadian tobacco bill.
newsitem.headline: Final Senate votes set on Canadian tobacco bill.

text.p: The Canadian Senate has scheduled a final series of votes for Wednesday evening on an anti-tobacco bill the government is rushing to push through Parliament before general elections, officials said Wednesday.

Parliament's elected chamber, the House of Commons, had passed the bill in March, but the Senate would also have to pass it before federal elections are called or the legislation would die. Prime Minister Jean Chretien is widely expected to call elections on April 27 or possibly a week later.
The bill would restrict tobacco company sponsorship of sporting and cultural events.

Introduced in response to a 1995 Supreme Court ruling that struck down a ban on tobacco ads, it would again seek to ban tobacco advertising through broadcasting or billboards and ban vending machine sales of tobacco.
A complication would be if the Senate passes any of the 27 amendments that have been proposed.
If so, the bill would revert to the House of Commons for debate, and if the House does not accept the amendments, the Senate would again have to vote on the bill.
But officials said the senators on both sides of the aisle voiced eagerness to push the legislation through ahead of the expected election call.
The votes were scheduled to start at 1730 EDT/2130 GMT.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain.

The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, is owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc (a unit of Rothmans International Plc, owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG ), and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Third place holder RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
